paragraphs: Under what general idea, then, should we understand the act that institutes government? I begin by observing that the act is complex, since it is made up of two others: the establishment of the law, and its execution.
By the first, the Sovereign decrees that a governing body shall be established in this or that form. This act is plainly a law.

By the second, the people names the rulers who will be entrusted with the government that has been established. This naming is a particular act. It is plainly not a second law, but only a consequence of the first and a function of government.

The difficulty is to see how there can be an act of government before government exists, and how the people, which is nothing but Sovereign or subjects, can in certain circumstances become a prince or magistrates.

Here one of the astonishing properties of the body politic comes to light, one by which it reconciles operations that seem to contradict each other. It does so through a sudden conversion of sovereignty into democracy. With no visible change, and simply through a new relation of all to all, the citizens become magistrates and pass from general acts to particular ones, from making law to carrying it out.

This change of relation is no mere theoretical subtlety without examples in practice. It happens every day in the English Parliament. On certain occasions the Lower House turns itself into a Grand Committee, so as to discuss business better. In that moment it goes from being a sovereign court to being a mere commission. Afterward it reports to itself, as the House of Commons, the results of its proceedings in Grand Committee, and debates again under one name what it has already settled under another.

It is, indeed, the particular advantage of democratic government that it can be established in fact by a simple act of the general will. After that, this provisional government stays in power if this form is adopted. Otherwise it establishes, in the name of the Sovereign, the government that the law prescribes, and so the whole procedure is regular. There is no other way to set up a government legitimately, in keeping with the principles laid down so far.
